free_tier.stated: No free tier. US-256-KVM (DC1) is USD 0.80 a quarter, or USD 2.80 a year, for 1 vCPU, 256 MB RAM, 2 GB SSD, 20 IPv4 NAT ports, one IPv6 /64 and 200 GB a month at 200 Mbps.

retention.stated: the server persists for the paid term; no deletion schedule is printed on the store or the configure page

egress.terms: 200 GB a month at 200 Mbps on the DC1 SKU, 50 GB at 300 Mbps on the SG-320 SKU; no overage price is printed

interface_detail: KVM guest with root; the public port block is derived from the internal address 10.10.10.N as N01-N20, the first port being SSH
tooling: any SSH client; the vendor runs a port calculator at port.virnat.com that returns the mapped ports from the internal IP
chaining: the second-cheapest documented-UDP machine in the band at USD 0.23 a month on annual prepay, with 256 MB and 19 usable TCP/UDP ports

limits.value: 200 GB a month on US-256-KVM DC1
20 forwarded ports on a shared IPv4, of which the first is TCP SSH and the remaining 19 forward the same port number, TCP or UDP

binding_note: 200 GB a month is the smallest traffic allowance in the band and the first thing a tunnel carrying real traffic exhausts.

identity_cost.detail: an account on the client area is required to order; the store and the configure page state no card hold and list no payment methods, so the rails are unverified.

reliability_note: no reliability event observed; the storefront and its port calculator are in Chinese while the store labels are in English, and no company, address or registration number appears on any page read
confidence_note: price, term, shape, traffic and the port rule are quoted from the vendor's own store and port-calculator pages read; the legal entity could not be established at all

evidence.proved: quoted card: 'US-256-KVM (DC1) | $0.80 USD /quarterly | 1 vCPU 256MB RAM 2GB SSD 20 IPv4 NAT Ports 1 /64 IPv6 Address 200GB @200Mbps per month KVM Virtualization'
quoted billing cycles: 'Billing Cycle $0.80 USD quarterly $2.80 USD annually'

quoted: '内网 IP 为 10.10.10.N 时，对应公网端口组为 N01-N20（例如 N=11 → 1101-1120）。其中第 1 个端口用于 TCP SSH → :22，其余 19 个端口按原端口转发，支持 TCP/UDP。' - the first port is TCP SSH to 22, the other 19 forward on the same port number and support TCP/UDP
quoted company-details table: 'Registered name | VirNAT', with 'Address | -', 'Telephone | -', 'Tax office | -', 'Tax number | -' - the entity fields are empty

notes: The best price-per-megabyte in the band after TierHive: USD 0.2333 a month on annual prepay for 256 MB, 2 GB of SSD, 200 GB of traffic, 20 NAT ports and a /64. The UDP statement is the cleanest found on any vendor page - the port calculator says in one sentence which port is SSH and that the other 19 carry TCP or UDP. What it does not have is a counterparty. The about page is a table with 'Registered name | VirNAT' and a dash in every other field: no address, no telephone, no tax number, no registration. The 200 GB allowance is also the tightest in the band. Not established: who operates it, whether the annual SKU renews at USD 2.80, and whether DC1 is in stock.

extras.term: 3 months at USD 0.80, or 12 months at USD 2.80
extras.price_arithmetic: USD 2.80 a year / 12 = USD 0.2333 a month on annual prepay; the quarterly cycle is USD 0.80 / 3 = USD 0.2667 a month. A VPS bills whether it runs or not, so the 24/7 and 10 h/day figures are the same.
extras.renewal_note: the configure page prints two cycles and no strike-through, so no promotional rate is stated and no renewal price is given

network_out.ports: 20 forwarded ports on a shared IPv4: 1 TCP SSH plus 19 that forward on the same port number, TCP or UDP; plus one IPv6 /64

extras.udp: stated: the port calculator says the 19 non-SSH ports '按原端口转发，支持 TCP/UDP' (forward on the same port number, supporting TCP/UDP)
extras.cart_evidence: configure page titled 'Configure: US-256-KVM (DC1)' renders 'Billing Cycle ... $0.80 USD quarterly ... $2.80 USD annually' and an Order Summary reading 'Product US-256-KVM (DC1) ... Add to Cart'
